topic: UI/UX Fundamentals, User Research, and Design Thinking
learningObjectives: Explain the differences between UI design and UX design.
Identify user needs through basic research and observation.
Apply design thinking stages to a digital product problem.

activities.title: UI vs UX Explorer
activities.instruction: Choose whether the activity is primarily UI or UX focused.

content.concept: UI focuses on the interface's visual and interactive elements, while UX focuses on the user's overall experience, needs, tasks, and problems.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

choices: Designing the visual style of a button
Observing users to discover why they struggle to complete checkout
config.answer: Designing the visual style of a button

activities.title: User Research Map
activities.instruction: Explore each research method and identify the type of insight it can provide.

content.concept: Interviews reveal motivations and opinions, surveys collect structured responses, observation reveals real behavior, and usability testing exposes interaction problems.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

descriptions: Useful for understanding motivations, expectations, frustrations, and opinions.
Useful for collecting structured responses from a larger group of users.
Useful for seeing how users actually behave in their real context.
Useful for identifying usability problems while users attempt specific tasks.

activities.title: Design Thinking Journey
activities.instruction: Arrange the common design thinking stages in the correct order.

content.concept: Design thinking commonly moves through empathizing with users, defining the problem, generating ideas, creating prototypes, and testing them. The process can be iterative.
content.tip: Interact with the example first. Your progress is saved for this session.

activities.title: Problem Framing Builder
activities.instruction: Build a focused user problem statement from the key parts.

content.concept: A useful problem statement identifies a specific user, their need or difficulty, and the context in which the problem occurs without prematurely prescribing a solution.
